items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: one of the numbers she featured was the version of Harry James "Carnival of red Venice"

ctx.x: Of course I did not play it after the band gad done it, but I told Glen that it was the'St. Louis Blues' even though he called it something else. And anyone that knew anything about jazz would have known it was what they had heard. After the discussion, they did not play it as long as I was touring with them and I featured it again.

The girl that played harmonica was very good and one of the numbers she featured was the version of Harry James "Carnival of red Venice". I regret that I did not mark her name in my little/book because she was the only female I ever heard that played jazz on harmonica.

Fred, Teddy, Glen and the girl singer spoke very good English and I always had one of them to help me choose something to eat in the reataurant and other things that I did not know how to ask for in German. Glen lived near Dormund and the night after we played there, we had the next day off. Glen invited the whole group to his home that day, That is, he invited everyone except me.
